title: How to Use a Small Vision Model as a Filter for an AI Agent
summary: Use a small vision model as a filter for your AI agent: run object detection in Roboflow Workflows and send only flagged images to the VLM.
body_markdown:
SUMMARY


**To use a small vision model as a filter for an AI agent, run an object detection model as a tool the agent calls first. The tool marks which images need review and returns boxes for the suspected issues, so the large vision model only looks at what was flagged. Build the filter in Roboflow Workflows and connect it to ChatGPT, Claude, or a custom Python agent.**


In a[manufacturing](https://roboflow.com/industries/manufacturing?ref=blog.roboflow.com) setting, inspection cameras capture images of products and components during production. Computer vision models can analyze these images for visible issues such as surface damage, missing components, or incorrect assembly. An AI agent can use the results to request further visual analysis and prepare a quality-control report.


As the number of inspection images grows, the agent needs a way to select images for detailed review. We can use an[object detection model (opens in a new tab)](https://playground.roboflow.com/models/task/object-detection?ref=blog.roboflow.com) as an image filter and expose it through a Workflow tool. The Workflow returns a selection flag, class labels, confidence scores, and bounding boxes. The agent uses these results to decide which images to review and which regions to inspect.


In this tutorial, we will build this filtering pipeline with Roboflow Workflows and use it as a tool for an AI agent. We will connect the Workflow through an existing agent application or a custom Python agent, then evaluate image filtering, token usage, and missed defects.


## How to Use a Small Vision Model as a Filter for an AI Agent


We will use textile manufacturing as our example. In fabric inspection, computer vision models can help locate holes and irregularities in the weave. Our example processes a batch of woven-fabric images to select regions that need closer review.


The Workflow runs object detection on each image and selects it for agent review when at least one retained defect prediction meets the confidence threshold. The agent then requests visual analysis and reports an assessment for each reviewed region.


Both options use an AI agent. In Option 1, an existing assistant in ChatGPT or Claude calls the Workflow and requests review through a separate VLM tool. In Option 2, a Python agent built with the OpenAI Agents SDK uses` gpt-6-sol` to call the tools and analyze the returned region crops.


We will use the public[fabric model on Roboflow Universe (opens in a new tab)](https://universe.roboflow.com/fabric-na8j5/fabric-kruoy?ref=blog.roboflow.com) . The checkpoint is` fabric-kruoy/18` , listed as RF-DETR Medium. The Workflow retains` fabric_broken_pick` ,` fabric_hole` ,` fabric_missing_pick` , and` fabric_thick_weft` . It excludes` fabric_perfect` from the review decision.


After building and testing the Workflow, we will use it as an AI agent tool through either of these methods:


Method and agent How the agent screens images How visual review works


Option 1: An assistant in ChatGPT or Claude, connected to Roboflow. The assistant calls` workflows_run` to run the Workflow. The assistant calls` media_analyze` for selected images. A separate vision model reviews the original image, and the assistant uses its analysis to prepare a report.


Option 2: A Python agent built with the OpenAI Agents SDK, using` gpt-6-sol` as its model. The agent calls` screen_fabric_images` to run the same Workflow. The agent calls` view_defect` to receive padded region crops. Its own model analyzes the crops and writes the report.


Choose Option 1 to use an assistant in ChatGPT or Claude with Roboflow tools for filtering and visual review. Choose Option 2 to build the agent in Python and process a local image folder. In both options, the Roboflow Workflow is the computer vision tool called by the agent. You can follow either option after completing the shared setup.


The Workflow contains the object detector and output-processing logic. The AI agent runs outside the Workflow. No large language model (LLM) or vision-language model (VLM) block is required inside it, and its output is JSON. A detection is a model prediction that still needs visual review. An image with no retained defect predictions is marked` not_selected` ; this does not establish that the fabric is defect-free.


The example Workflow is[textile-defect-agent-filter](https://app.roboflow.com/workflows/embed/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ3b3JrZmxvd0lkIjoiZnhNNEJzYW5GMlQ3OHN1ZzNEdGYiLCJ3b3Jrc3BhY2VJZCI6InZjQmw1Y0x3bUtQallLTGNRemV1VkE4UlRhNjIiLCJ1c2VySWQiOiJ2Y0JsNWNMd21LUGpZS0xjUXpldVZBOFJUYTYyIiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzMTk2NzkzfQ.MT06MV1rixRNaXJ2Y7drqitKE8nSxDmQ2NBMYw0UMDY?ref=blog.roboflow.com) in workspace` tim-4ijf0` . That link opens the example workspace's editor. Readers using another workspace should build their own copy and replace the workspace and Workflow identifiers in the examples.


### Step 1: Prepare a fabric image test set


Select a small set of fabric images with verified defect labels and a consistent orientation. Include clear defects, subtle defects, and images verified as acceptable by an inspector. Keep the original image files unchanged after inference so the returned bounding-box coordinates remain valid.


For Option 1, use a direct HTTPS image URL that Roboflow can access for both Workflow inference and VLM review. Provide the URL as text. Attaching the image directly to the conversation may send it to the chat model before filtering.


For Option 2, place JPG, JPEG, PNG, or WEBP files in a local folder named` fabric-images` . The supplied program also reads subfolders. It uses each file's relative path as` image_id` , such as` roll-01/frame-003.jpg` , so files with the same name in different subfolders remain distinct.


Keep the verified labels and inspection notes in a separate record. We will use them to evaluate the complete pipeline.


### Step 2: Build the textile defect detection Workflow


In your Roboflow workspace, select Workflows, create a new Workflow, and choose Build from scratch. Name it` textile-defect-agent-filter` . The[Workflow creation guide (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/build/create-a-workflow?ref=blog.roboflow.com) explains how to open a blank Workflow.


Add the components shown below. The main branch runs object detection, counts the retained predictions, and creates the review flag. The remaining connections supply the original image dimensions and image identifier to the result formatter.


**Roboflow**[Workflow for textile defect screening](https://app.roboflow.com/workflows/embed/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ3b3JrZmxvd0lkIjoiZnhNNEJzYW5GMlQ3OHN1ZzNEdGYiLCJ3b3Jrc3BhY2VJZCI6InZjQmw1Y0x3bUtQallLTGNRemV1VkE4UlRhNjIiLCJ1c2VySWQiOiJ2Y0JsNWNMd21LUGpZS0xjUXpldVZBOFJUYTYyIiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzMjkwMzQ2fQ.WOqAIhHD1-pug_KFTXQC8BUBItAL2V-gBvlVncUftc4?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **. The Workflow detects possible defects and returns a selection flag, bounding boxes, and detection metadata for the AI agent.**


**Configure the inputs**


Add one image input and two parameters:


Name Type Purpose and default


` image` Image The original fabric image used for inference.


` image_id` Text parameter The identifier returned with the result. Default: an empty string.


` confidence_threshold` Number parameter The minimum detection score to retain. Default: 0.25.


Supply a unique` image_id` on every request to associate each result with its input image. The Workflow accepts an empty default, but a unique identifier makes batch results easier to track. Start with a confidence threshold of` 0.25` and evaluate it on your test set.


**Add the object detection model**


Add an[Object Detection Model block (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks/run-a-model/object-detection-model?ref=blog.roboflow.com) and name it` detect_textile_defects` . Configure these connections and settings:


Setting Value


Image input` $inputs.image`


Model ID` fabric-kruoy/18`


Confidence mode Custom


Custom confidence` $inputs.confidence_threshold`


Set the class filter to:


```text
[
"fabric_broken_pick",
"fabric_hole",
"fabric_missing_pick",
"fabric_thick_weft"
]
```


The model block retains qualifying predictions for these four classes.` fabric_perfect` does not contribute to the review decision. If an image contains both a retained defect and a` fabric_perfect` prediction, the retained defect still selects it for review.


The class and confidence filters are configured in this model block, so this Workflow does not require a separate Detections Filter block. Its prediction output is` $steps.detect_textile_defects.predictions` .


The confidence value is a model score. A threshold of` 0.25` does not mean the material has a 25% chance of being defective.


**Count the retained predictions**


Add a[Property Definition block (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks/advanced-blocks/property-definition?ref=blog.roboflow.com) named` count_defect_detections` .


Set its data input to` $steps.detect_textile_defects.predictions` . Use Count Items, represented by the` SequenceLength` operation in the saved definition. Its output,` $steps.count_defect_detections.output` , is the number of retained defect predictions.


This count determines whether the image is selected for review. It represents the number of retained bounding boxes. It does not measure defect severity or the number of defective fabric rolls.


**Create the review flag and selection reason**


Add two[Expression blocks (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks/advanced-blocks/expression?ref=blog.roboflow.com) . In both blocks, create an input variable named` count` and connect it to` $steps.count_defect_detections.output` .


Name the first block` select_for_agent_review` . Add a case that checks whether` count` is greater than` 0` . Return the Boolean value` true` when it matches, and set the default result to the Boolean value` false` .


Name the second block` set_review_reason` . Use the same condition, but return the text` possible_defect` when it matches and` not_selected` as the default result.


Retained defect count Review flag Selection reason


Greater than 0` true`` possible_defect`


0` false`` not_selected`


Use Boolean values for the flag, rather than the strings` "true"` and` "false"` . The formatter receives the flag from` $steps.select_for_agent_review.output` and the reason from` $steps.set_review_reason.output` .


Both outcomes continue to the formatter. Keeping a result for an image with zero retained detections allows the caller to account for that image in the batch.


**Read the original image dimensions**


Add two more Property Definition blocks, both reading` $inputs.image` :


Block name Operation Property


` get_original_image_width`` ExtractImageProperty`` width`


` get_original_image_height`` ExtractImageProperty`` height`


The width and height describe the original input image and provide the reference dimensions for the bounding boxes. The Workflow passes the original image to the detector without an earlier crop or transformation block.


**Add the result formatter**


Add a[custom Python block (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/blocks/blocks/custom-blocks?ref=blog.roboflow.com) with the block type` Textile_Result_Formatter` and the step name` format_agent_review_json` .


Create the following inputs. The prediction input accepts object detection predictions. The remaining inputs receive the parameter or step outputs shown in the table.


Formatter input Connect to


` predictions`` $steps.detect_textile_defects.predictions`


` image_id`` $inputs.image_id`


` width`` $steps.get_original_image_width.output`


` height`` $steps.get_original_image_height.output`


` defect_count`` $steps.count_defect_detections.output`


` selected`` $steps.select_for_agent_review.output`


` reason`` $steps.set_review_reason.output`


Define one output named` result` with the kind` dictionary` , then use this run function in` format_agent_review_json` . It matches the uploaded formatter code, laid out for readability. Renaming the step changes its selectors; the function arguments and returned JSON fields stay the same. The[dynamic Python block reference (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/developer-guide/developer-guide/dynamic-python-blocks?ref=blog.roboflow.com) explains the input/output definitions and supplies` math` as a baseline import.


Python


```text
def   run  (self, predictions, image_id, width, height,
defect_count, selected, reason):
w, h   =   int  (width),   int  (height)
if   w   <=   0   or   h   <=   0  :
raise   ValueError  (  "Invalid original image dimensions"  )


n   =   len  (predictions)
if   n   !=   int  (defect_count):
raise   ValueError  (  "Detection count mismatch"  )


names   =   list  (predictions.data.get(  "class_name"  , []))
scores   =   predictions.confidence
allowed   =   {
"fabric_broken_pick"  ,   "fabric_hole"  ,
"fabric_missing_pick"  ,   "fabric_thick_weft"
}
rows   =   []
if   n   >   0   and   (  len  (names)   !=   n   or   scores   is   None   or   len  (scores)   !=   n):
raise   ValueError  (  "Missing prediction classes or confidence scores"  )


for   i, box   in   enumerate  (predictions.xyxy):
name   =   str  (names[i])
confidence   =   float  (scores[i])
coords   =   [  float  (v)   for   v   in   box]
if   (name   not   in   allowed   or   not   math.isfinite(confidence)
or   not   all  (math.isfinite(v)   for   v   in   coords)):
raise   ValueError  (  "Invalid defect prediction"  )
rows.append({
"class"  : name,
"confidence"  : confidence,
"bbox"  : {
"x_min"  : coords[  0  ],   "y_min"  : coords[  1  ],
"x_max"  : coords[  2  ],   "y_max"  : coords[  3  ]
}
})


return   {
"result"  : {
"processing_status"  :   "success"  ,
"image_id"  :   str  (image_id),
"selected_for_review"  :   bool  (selected),
"reason"  :   str  (reason),
"defect_count"  : n,
"image_dimensions"  : {  "width"  : w,   "height"  : h},
"coordinate_format"  : {
"format"  :   "xyxy"  ,   "units"  :   "pixels"  ,
"reference"  :   "original_image"  ,   "origin"  :   "top_left"  ,
"x_direction"  :   "right"  ,   "y_direction"  :   "down"
},
"predictions"  : rows
}
}
```


The formatter validates the dimensions, prediction count, class labels, and numeric values before creating the output dictionary. These checks validate the output structure. Visual analysis is still required to assess each predicted defect.


Each prediction includes its class, confidence, and an **xyxy** box. The two corners are` x_min, y_min` and` x_max, y_max` , measured in original-image pixels from the top-left. The final two values are corner coordinates, not the box's width and height.


**Configure the Workflow output**


Add one Workflow output named` result` and connect it to` $steps.format_agent_review_json.result` .


The result contains` processing_status` ,` image_id` ,` selected_for_review` ,` reason` ,` defect_count` ,` image_dimensions` ,` coordinate_format` , and` predictions` . Return JSON only from the Workflow. Keep the original image URL or local file path available so the agent can access the image after selection.


Save the[Workflow](https://app.roboflow.com/workflows/embed/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ3b3JrZmxvd0lkIjoiZnhNNEJzYW5GMlQ3OHN1ZzNEdGYiLCJ3b3Jrc3BhY2VJZCI6InZjQmw1Y0x3bUtQallLTGNRemV1VkE4UlRhNjIiLCJ1c2VySWQiOiJ2Y0JsNWNMd21LUGpZS0xjUXpldVZBOFJUYTYyIiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzMjkwMzQ2fQ.WOqAIhHD1-pug_KFTXQC8BUBItAL2V-gBvlVncUftc4?ref=blog.roboflow.com) before moving to the image tests.


**The**[textile defect screening Workflow](https://app.roboflow.com/workflows/embed/eyJhbGciOiJIUzI1NiIsInR5cCI6IkpXVCJ9.eyJ3b3JrZmxvd0lkIjoiZnhNNEJzYW5GMlQ3OHN1ZzNEdGYiLCJ3b3Jrc3BhY2VJZCI6InZjQmw1Y0x3bUtQallLTGNRemV1VkE4UlRhNjIiLCJ1c2VySWQiOiJ2Y0JsNWNMd21LUGpZS0xjUXpldVZBOFJUYTYyIiwiaWF0IjoxNzkzMjkwMzQ2fQ.WOqAIhHD1-pug_KFTXQC8BUBItAL2V-gBvlVncUftc4?ref=blog.roboflow.com) **in the Roboflow editor, using the same descriptive block names as the tutorial.**


### Step 3: Test the Workflow and inspect the JSON


Open the Workflow editor's Run panel, supply an image and an` image_id` , and run the Workflow with` confidence_threshold` set to` 0.25` . The[Workflow testing guide (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/build/test-a-workflow?ref=blog.roboflow.com) explains how to inspect the structured output.


Here is a previously recorded response from the example Workflow for image` 26f5127e5487946d0079` . This is a different input from the public Universe test image used in Step 4, so its predictions are an example of the output format:


JSON


```text
[
{
"result"  : {
"processing_status"  :   "success"  ,
"image_id"  :   "26f5127e5487946d0079"  ,
"selected_for_review"  :   true  ,
"reason"  :   "possible_defect"  ,
"defect_count"  :   1  ,
"image_dimensions"  : {
"width"  :   2464  ,
"height"  :   2048
},
"coordinate_format"  : {
"format"  :   "xyxy"  ,
"units"  :   "pixels"  ,
"reference"  :   "original_image"  ,
"origin"  :   "top_left"  ,
"x_direction"  :   "right"  ,
"y_direction"  :   "down"
},
"predictions"  : [
{
"class"  :   "fabric_hole"  ,
"confidence"  :   0.26379328966140747  ,
"bbox"  : {
"x_min"  :   1626  ,
"y_min"  :   66  ,
"x_max"  :   2085  ,
"y_max"  :   494
}
}
]
}
}
]
```


The outer list contains one image result. Inside` result` ,` processing_status: "success"` means screening completed. The Workflow retained one` fabric_hole` prediction with a confidence score of approximately` 0.264` , which exceeds the configured` 0.25` threshold. It therefore returned` selected_for_review: true` .


The box runs from` (1626, 66)` to` (2085, 494)` in the original 2464 × 2048 image. These are two corner coordinates, not a position followed by width and height. The confidence score belongs to the detector; it does not confirm that a hole is present.


**Coordinate schematic for the recorded Workflow response. The predicted region extends from (1626, 66) to (2085, 494) in the original 2464 × 2048 image.**


Test an image verified as acceptable and an image with a subtle defect. Compare the predicted bounding boxes with the verified defect locations. When inference succeeds with no retained predictions, the result should contain` selected_for_review: false` ,` reason: "not_selected"` ,` defect_count: 0` , and an empty` predictions` list. A processing failure must produce an execution error.


This response demonstrates one successful Workflow inference run. Test agent tool execution and visual analysis separately. Measuring accuracy or token reduction requires an evaluation dataset and comparison runs.


After testing,[save and publish the Workflow (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows/build/build-a-workflow?ref=blog.roboflow.com#saving-changes) . The MCP tool uses the latest published version, so publish any changes you intend the agent to use.


### Step 4: Use the Workflow as an AI Agent Tool


The published Workflow is ready to run object detection and return structured results. The next step is to make it callable by an AI agent. The agent sends an inference request through a tool, reads the JSON response, and uses the selected predictions to guide visual analysis.


The output has two roles.` selected_for_review` controls which images enter the analysis stage. The` predictions` array supplies the class labels, confidence scores, and bounding boxes for each selected image.


**The Workflow returns an image-selection flag and detection metadata. The agent uses these outputs to select images for review and locate regions of interest.**


Choose one of the following integrations. In Option 1, an assistant in ChatGPT or Claude calls the Workflow and requests VLM review through a second Roboflow tool. In Option 2, a Python agent built with the OpenAI Agents SDK calls the Workflow through a function tool, then uses its own model,` gpt-6-sol` , to analyze returned region crops. Both rely on the retained predictions: a missed detection can exclude a defective image from review, and region crops can omit other defects in the same image.


### Option 1: Use ChatGPT or Claude as the AI agent


We use an existing AI assistant in ChatGPT or Claude as the agent, with the Roboflow connection enabled. The agent calls` workflows_run` to screen the image. When the result selects the image, it calls the separate` media_analyze` VLM tool for visual review. That tool loads the original image and asks a vision model to assess it. The agent uses the returned analysis to prepare the inspection report.


This method does not depend on the chat client's ability to open an external image directly. The visual review happens through a separate tool, outside the detection Workflow. The[Roboflow MCP guide (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/agents/mcp-server?ref=blog.roboflow.com) lists both tools and the supported connection methods.


The review tool receives the full original image. The bounding boxes in its question guide the visual analysis. Option 2 provides explicit region crops when you need that control over the image input.


**Option 1: an assistant in ChatGPT or Claude calls the Workflow to screen images, uses a separate VLM tool to review selected images, and prepares the inspection report.**


### 1. Enable the Roboflow tools


In ChatGPT, install the[Roboflow plugin (opens in a new tab)](https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6ac2713d52dc8191913b283379e39840?ref=blog.roboflow.com) and sign in when prompted. In Claude, use the Roboflow connector linked in the[MCP setup guide (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/agents/mcp-server?ref=blog.roboflow.com) . If your client is already connected to the correct workspace, check that it exposes both` workflows_run` and` media_analyze` . Tool names may include a client-specific prefix.


The connected account must have access to your published Workflow and permission to use both tools. If you built your own copy, replace the workspace and Workflow identifiers below. Roboflow must also be able to retrieve the image URL. Pasting the prompt into a chat without the connected tools will not execute the process.


` media_analyze` uses workspace credits for a vision-model call. We call it only for selected images. The detection Workflow remains JSON-only and has no LLM or VLM block.


### 2. Request filtering followed by visual review


Use this prompt with an original image from the[fabric dataset on Roboflow Universe (opens in a new tab)](https://universe.roboflow.com/fabric-na8j5/fabric-kruoy?ref=blog.roboflow.com) . The dataset lists image` NM0YAb5kjVesmskIj3Be` in its test split with one` fabric_hole` annotation. This is a reference label. Inference and visual review must produce their own results.


` Image URL` points directly to the JPEG file.` image_id` is a tracking label returned unchanged by the Workflow. We use the dataset image ID here, but another unique label also works. Enable the Roboflow tools for the conversation and paste this prompt:


```text
Use the Roboflow tools to inspect this fabric image.


Workspace: tim-4ijf0
Workflow ID: textile-defect-agent-filter-1793090127138
Image URL: https://source.roboflow.com/jCsmAr4784Mgz4kk6OH9ETCa6BD2/NM0YAb5kjVesmskIj3Be/original.jpg
image_id: NM0YAb5kjVesmskIj3Be
confidence_threshold: 0.25


First call workflows_run with the image URL, image_id, and threshold.
Do not request visual analysis before reading its result.


If processing fails, report the execution error separately.
If selected_for_review is false, report not_selected and stop.
Do not describe an unselected image as verified defect-free.


If selected_for_review is true, call media_analyze with the same URL
and media_type=image. In its question, include the original image
dimensions and every returned class, confidence score, and xyxy box.
Ask the vision model to inspect those regions and surrounding texture,
describe the visible evidence, and assess each prediction as
visually_supported, not_supported, or uncertain. Treat the detector
outputs as unverified predictions, including high-confidence ones.


Use the returned visual analysis to write the report. If the tool is
unavailable, fails, or cannot inspect a region, mark that region
not_reviewed and explain why. Use uncertain only when an image was
inspected but the visual evidence was inconclusive.


Keep detector results separate from VLM assessments. Do not infer
appearance from JSON or treat a model assessment as physical confirmation.
Return short bullet points with the image ID, screening result, detector
predictions, review tool, visual assessment, evidence, and next action
for a human inspector.
```


The Workflow sets the selection flag. The agent's instructions use that flag to request the second tool call. The Workflow itself does not start the visual review.


### 3. Check both tool calls


The first call runs the published Workflow:


```text
{
"workflow_id": "textile-defect-agent-filter-1793090127138",
"images": {
"image": "https://source.roboflow.com/jCsmAr4784Mgz4kk6OH9ETCa6BD2/NM0YAb5kjVesmskIj3Be/original.jpg"
},
"parameters": {
"image_id": "NM0YAb5kjVesmskIj3Be",
"confidence_threshold": 0.25
}
}
```


The workspace comes from the Roboflow connection. The Workflow ID is its URL slug. After a successful result with` selected_for_review: true` , the conversation should show a` media_analyze` call. Its question should use the dimensions and predictions from that execution.


For the screening result reported for this test image, the review call has this form:


```text
{
"url": "https://source.roboflow.com/jCsmAr4784Mgz4kk6OH9ETCa6BD2/NM0YAb5kjVesmskIj3Be/original.jpg",
"media_type": "image",
"question": "Visually review the predicted region in this 2048 x 1536 fabric image. The detector suggested fabric_hole with confidence 0.6238 at xyxy [328, 640, 565, 914], measured in original-image pixels from the top-left. Inspect this region and the surrounding weave. Describe the visible evidence and assess the prediction as visually_supported, not_supported, or uncertain. Treat the detector output as an unverified prediction. If you cannot inspect the image or region, report not_reviewed and explain why. Do not assess the rest of the fabric as defect-free."
}
```


This second JSON example uses values reported for this input. For another image or a new inference result, use its returned values. The coordinates in Step 3 belong to a different image.


` media_analyze` returns a structured analysis with a summary. The requested assessment labels belong in the agent's report; they are not new fields in the Workflow output. Use the tool's visual observations to assess the selected predictions. Keep the Workflow's class labels and detection count separate from any additional model recommendations.


### 4. Interpret the review result


For this image, the reported Workflow run returned one` fabric_hole` prediction with confidence` 0.6238` , a bounding box of` \[328, 640, 565, 914\]` , and` selected_for_review: true` . Its dimensions were 2048 × 1536 pixels.


A subsequent live` media_analyze` call successfully loaded the image. The vision model assessed the region as **visually supported** and described a localized disruption in the weave, broken yarn, and a small opening. This is a VLM assessment for human review, not confirmation from a physical inspection.


The earlier image-access error occurred after Workflow inference had succeeded. It meant that the client could not complete its own image-viewing step. Calling the review tool resolved that step in this test. The successful review call is recorded in` visual-review-test-result.json` in the tutorial files. This does not establish accuracy across a dataset or compatibility in every client.


When image loading or review fails, report not reviewed. Use uncertain when the review actually ran but the visual evidence was inconclusive. Keep either outcome separate from` processing_status: "success"` , which only describes the Workflow execution.


### Option 2: Build a Python agent with the OpenAI Agents SDK


We create a custom agent in Python using the[OpenAI Agents SDK (opens in a new tab)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/sdk?ref=blog.roboflow.com) . The same agent model analyzes those crops and writes the inspection report.


The SDK manages the agent's tool-calling loop: it executes each function requested by the model and returns the tool output for the next model turn. The Workflow supplies the detection results, and the viewing tool supplies the image crops.


**Option 2: a Python agent built with the OpenAI Agents SDK uses GPT-6 Sol to call the Workflow tool, request selected region crops, analyze them, and write the report.**


The first tool sends image data to Roboflow for inference. It returns counts, image identifiers, and detection metadata to the agent model. The second tool supplies image data when the agent requests a selected region.

### 2. Add the imports and response validation


The settings identify the published Workflow.` validate_result` checks the image identifier, prediction count, selection flag, and bounding-box coordinates. An invalid response is recorded as a processing error.


Python


```text
"""Use a published Roboflow Workflow as a tool for a Python inspection agent."""


import   argparse
import   base64
import   io
import   json
import   math
import   os
import   time
from   datetime   import   datetime
from   pathlib   import   Path


from   agents   import   (
Agent, ModelSettings, RunConfig, Runner, ToolOutputImage, ToolOutputText,
function_tool, set_default_openai_api,
)
from   inference_sdk   import   InferenceConfiguration, InferenceHTTPClient
from   PIL   import   Image


WORKSPACE   =   "tim-4ijf0"
WORKFLOW_ID   =   "textile-defect-agent-filter-1793090127138"
IMAGE_TYPES   =   {  ".jpg"  ,   ".jpeg"  ,   ".png"  ,   ".webp"  }
DEFECT_CLASSES   =   {
"fabric_broken_pick"  ,   "fabric_hole"  ,
"fabric_missing_pick"  ,   "fabric_thick_weft"  ,
}
CROP_MAX_SIDE   =   1024


def   validate_result  (response, image_id):
"""Reject inconsistent screening data before offering it to the agent."""
if   not   isinstance  (response,   list  )   or   len  (response)   !=   1  :
raise   ValueError  (  "Expected one Workflow result"  )
result   =   response[  0  ][  "result"  ]
if   (result[  "processing_status"  ]   !=   "success"
or   result[  "image_id"  ]   !=   image_id):
raise   ValueError  (  "Unsuccessful or mismatched result"  )
predictions, count   =   result[  "predictions"  ], result[  "defect_count"  ]
if   (  not   isinstance  (predictions,   list  )   or   type  (count)   is   not   int
or   count   !=   len  (predictions)):
raise   ValueError  (  "Invalid prediction count"  )
selected   =   result[  "selected_for_review"  ]
if   type  (selected)   is   not   bool   or   selected   !=   (count   >   0  ):
raise   ValueError  (  "Invalid review decision"  )
if   result[  "reason"  ]   !=   (  "possible_defect"   if   selected   else   "not_selected"  ):
raise   ValueError  (  "Invalid selection reason"  )
dims   =   result[  "image_dimensions"  ]
if   any  (  type  (dims[k])   is   not   int   or   dims[k]   <=   0   for   k   in   (  "width"  ,   "height"  )):
raise   ValueError  (  "Invalid image dimensions"  )
expected   =   {  "format"  :   "xyxy"  ,   "units"  :   "pixels"  ,   "reference"  :   "original_image"  ,
"origin"  :   "top_left"  ,   "x_direction"  :   "right"  ,   "y_direction"  :   "down"  }
if   any  (result[  "coordinate_format"  ].get(k)   !=   v   for   k, v   in   expected.items()):
raise   ValueError  (  "Unexpected coordinate format"  )
for   hint   in   predictions:
score   =   float  (hint[  "confidence"  ])
box   =   hint[  "bbox"  ]
x1, y1, x2, y2   =   [  float  (box[k])   for   k   in   (  "x_min"  ,   "y_min"  ,   "x_max"  ,   "y_max"  )]
if   (hint[  "class"  ]   not   in   DEFECT_CLASSES   or   not   math.isfinite(score)
or   not   0   <=   score   <=   1
or   not   all  (math.isfinite(v)   for   v   in   (x1, y1, x2, y2))
or   not   x1   <   x2   or   not   y1   <   y2
or   x2   <=   0   or   y2   <=   0   or   x1   >=   dims[  "width"  ]   or   y1   >=   dims[  "height"  ]):
raise   ValueError  (  "Invalid defect hint"  )
return   result
```


The returned` bbox` is a dictionary. Read its named fields, such as` box\["x_min"\]` ; unpacking the dictionary itself would read its keys instead of the numeric coordinates.


### 3. Add the inference and image-viewing tools


` build_tools` configures both tools with the image folder, confidence threshold, and Roboflow client. The agent receives the tool definitions. The Python program stores local file paths and inference results, then returns the requested data through tool outputs.


Python


```text
def   build_tools  (folder, client, confidence  =  0.25  ,
workspace  =  WORKSPACE  , workflow_id  =  WORKFLOW_ID  ):
"""Keep each run's files and results in its own local state."""
folder   =   Path(folder).resolve()
if   not   folder.is_dir()   or   not   math.isfinite(confidence)   or   not   0   <=   confidence   <=   1  :
raise   ValueError  (  "Provide an existing folder and confidence from 0 to 1"  )
paths   =   sorted  (p   for   p   in   folder.rglob(  "*"  )
if   p.is_file()   and   p.suffix.lower()   in   IMAGE_TYPES  )
if   not   paths:
raise   ValueError  (  "No supported image files found"  )
selected_files   =   {}
state   =   {  "summary"  :   None  ,   "records"  : [],   "views"  : [],   "view_errors"  : []}


@function_tool
def   screen_fabric_images  () ->   str  :
"""Screen the configured folder with Roboflow before viewing any image.


Returns JSON counts, selected-image hints and processing errors.
No image pixels are returned. Repeated calls reuse this run's results.
"""
if   state[  "summary"  ]   is   not   None  :
return   json.dumps(state[  "summary"  ])
print  (  "[tool] screen_fabric_images"  )
selected, errors   =   [], []
for   path   in   paths:
image_id   =   path.relative_to(folder).as_posix()
try  :
response   =   client.run_workflow(
workspace_name  =  workspace,   workflow_id  =  workflow_id,
images  =  {  "image"  :   str  (path)},
parameters  =  {  "image_id"  : image_id,
"confidence_threshold"  : confidence},
use_cache  =  False  ,
)
result   =   validate_result(response, image_id)
state[  "records"  ].append({  "path"  :   str  (path),   "result"  : result})
if   result[  "selected_for_review"  ]:
selected_files[image_id]   =   (path, result)
selected.append({
"image_id"  : image_id,
"image_dimensions"  : result[  "image_dimensions"  ],
"hints"  : [{  "defect_index"  : i,   **  hint}
for   i, hint   in   enumerate  (result[  "predictions"  ])],
})
except   Exception   as   exc:
errors.append({  "image_id"  : image_id,   "error_type"  :   type  (exc).  __name__  })
state[  "summary"  ]   =   {
"images_total"  :   len  (paths),   "screened"  :   len  (state[  "records"  ]),
"selected_count"  :   len  (selected),
"not_selected"  :   len  (state[  "records"  ])   -   len  (selected),
"selected"  : selected,   "processing_errors"  : errors,
}
return   json.dumps(state[  "summary"  ])


@function_tool
def   view_defect  (image_id:   str  , defect_index:   int  ) -> list[ToolOutputText   |   ToolOutputImage]:
"""Show one padded region from an image selected by screen_fabric_images.


Args:
image_id: An identifier in the screening tool's selected list.
defect_index: The zero-based hint index returned by that tool.
"""
print  (  f  "[tool] view_defect:   {  image_id  }  , hint   {  defect_index  }  "  )
try  :
path, result   =   selected_files[image_id]
data_url, bounds, size   =   make_crop(path, result, defect_index)
record   =   {  "image_id"  : image_id,   "defect_index"  : defect_index,
"crop_xyxy"  :   list  (bounds),   "display_size"  :   list  (size)}
state[  "views"  ].append(record)
return   [ToolOutputText(  text  =  json.dumps(record)),
ToolOutputImage(  image_url  =  data_url,   detail  =  "high"  )]
except   Exception   as   exc:
record   =   {  "image_id"  : image_id,   "defect_index"  : defect_index,
"error_type"  :   type  (exc).  __name__  }
state[  "view_errors"  ].append(record)
return   [ToolOutputText(  text  =  json.dumps({  "view_error"  : record}))]


return   [screen_fabric_images, view_defect], state
```


The` @function_tool` decorator makes each function available to the agent. The function name, parameter types, and docstring describe the tool's inputs and purpose. The tools become callable by this agent when we pass them to its` tools` list below. See the[agent definitions guide (opens in a new tab)](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/agents/define-agents?ref=blog.roboflow.com) .


The screening tool processes one image at a time through the[Roboflow Inference SDK (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/reference/inference/inference-sdk/workflows?ref=blog.roboflow.com) .` use_cache=False` avoids reusing a recently cached Workflow definition during testing. Keep the published version fixed while comparing results.


Every successful inference result is stored in the local audit record. Only selected images enter` selected_files` and the` selected` list returned to the agent. The` hints` field contains each prediction's class, confidence score, and bounding box. Each prediction also receives a zero-based` defect_index` , which identifies the region to request. Inference errors remain separate from successful` not_selected` results.


The second tool uses` image_id` and` defect_index` to retrieve a region from the selected records. It rejects requests for unselected images. Repeated calls to the first tool return the stored results for that run.


### 4. Create the region-of-interest crop


The viewing tool calls this helper to crop the region of interest. It reads the bounding box in original-image pixels, adds padding for visual context, and clips the crop coordinates to the image boundaries.


Python


```text
def   make_crop  (path, result, defect_index):
"""Read named xyxy coordinates and return a bounded crop as a data URL."""
if   not   0   <=   defect_index   <   len  (result[  "predictions"  ]):
raise   ValueError  (  "Unknown defect index"  )
box   =   result[  "predictions"  ][defect_index][  "bbox"  ]
with   Image.open(path)   as   source:
image   =   source.convert(  "RGB"  )
dims   =   result[  "image_dimensions"  ]
if   image.size   !=   (dims[  "width"  ], dims[  "height"  ]):
raise   ValueError  (  "Original image dimensions changed"  )
pad_x   =   0.25   *   (x2   -   x1)   +   32
pad_y   =   0.25   *   (y2   -   y1)   +   32
bounds   =   (  max  (  0  , math.floor(x1   -   pad_x)),   max  (  0  , math.floor(y1   -   pad_y)),
min  (image.width, math.ceil(x2   +   pad_x)),
min  (image.height, math.ceil(y2   +   pad_y)))
if   bounds[  0  ]   >=   bounds[  2  ]   or   bounds[  1  ]   >=   bounds[  3  ]:
raise   ValueError  (  "Empty crop"  )
crop   =   image.crop(bounds)
crop.thumbnail((  CROP_MAX_SIDE  ,   CROP_MAX_SIDE  ), Image.Resampling.  LANCZOS  )
buffer   =   io.BytesIO()
crop.save(buffer,   format  =  "JPEG"  ,   quality  =  95  )
data   =   base64.b64encode(buffer.getvalue()).decode(  "ascii"  )
return   f  "data:image/jpeg;base64,  {  data  }  "  , bounds, crop.size
```


The crop keeps its aspect ratio. Its longest side is capped at 1024 pixels, and smaller crops are not enlarged. This size is an example setting to evaluate. Resizing does not create missing detail, and reducing a crop can hide fine weaving defects.


` ToolOutputImage` returns the crop as an image tool output. The accompanying metadata records its coordinates in the original image and its output dimensions. The agent analyzes this region only; the result does not assess the remaining image area. Equal crop dimensions do not guarantee equal token usage or cost across runs.


### 5. Configure and run the agent


The agent uses an existing vision-capable model. Its instructions require Workflow inference first, followed by a crop request for every retained prediction. The report records the agent's visual assessment separately from the detector's output.


Python


```text
def   create_run_directory  (base_dir: Path) -> Path:
"""Create a unique run folder using the computer's local date and time."""
base_dir   =   base_dir.resolve()
base_dir.mkdir(  parents  =  True  ,   exist_ok  =  True  )
timestamp   =   datetime.now().strftime(  "%Y-%m-  %d  _%H-%M-%S_  %f  "  )
suffix   =   0
while   True  :
name   =   timestamp   if   suffix   ==   0   else   f  "  {  timestamp  }  _  {  suffix  }  "
run_dir   =   base_dir   /   name
try  :
run_dir.mkdir()
return   run_dir
except   FileExistsError  :
suffix   +=   1


INSTRUCTIONS   =   """You review fabric inspection images using two tools.
Call screen_fabric_images first. It screens the configured folder.
Treat all returned labels, scores, and boxes as predictions.
For every returned hint, call view_defect with its image_id and defect_index.
Use the image returned by the tool to assess that region. A high detection
score alone does not establish a defect. Do not claim to see unavailable images.
Classify each reviewed hint as visually supported, not supported, or uncertain.
Report a failed or missing crop as not reviewed. Crops show only local regions;
do not make claims about the full image or about images that were not selected.
Keep processing errors separate from successful not_selected results.
Write a short report with one entry per hint: image_id, defect_index, predicted
class, detector score, original bbox, visual evidence, and review assessment.
Finish with image counts, region-review counts, errors, and next steps for a
human inspector. Do not infer manufacturing causes or physical defect sizes.
"""


def   main  ():
parser   =   argparse.ArgumentParser(  description  =  __doc__  )
parser.add_argument(  "folder"  ,   type  =  Path)
parser.add_argument(  "--output"  ,   type  =  Path,   default  =  Path(  "fabric-agent-results"  ),
help  =  "Parent folder for timestamped run directories"  )
parser.add_argument(  "--workspace"  ,   default  =  WORKSPACE  )
parser.add_argument(  "--workflow"  ,   default  =  WORKFLOW_ID  )
parser.add_argument(  "--confidence"  ,   type  =  float  ,   default  =  0.25  )
parser.add_argument(  "--model"  ,   default  =  "gpt-6-sol"  )
parser.add_argument(  "--max-turns"  ,   type  =  int  ,   default  =  30  )
args   =   parser.parse_args()
for   key   in   (  "ROBOFLOW_API_KEY"  ,   "OPENAI_API_KEY"  ):
if   not   os.environ.get(key):
parser.error(  f  "Configure   {  key  }   privately in this terminal"  )
client   =   InferenceHTTPClient(
api_url  =  "https://serverless.roboflow.com"  ,
api_key  =  os.environ[  "ROBOFLOW_API_KEY"  ],
).configure(InferenceConfiguration(  api_key_transport  =  "header"  ))
tools, state   =   build_tools(args.folder, client, args.confidence,
args.workspace, args.workflow)
output_dir   =   create_run_directory(args.output)
print  (  f  "[output]   {  output_dir  }  "  )
set_default_openai_api(  "responses"  )
agent   =   Agent(  name  =  "Fabric inspection agent"  ,   model  =  args.model,
instructions  =  INSTRUCTIONS  ,   tools  =  tools,
model_settings  =  ModelSettings(  parallel_tool_calls  =  False  ))
started   =   time.perf_counter()
try  :
result   =   Runner.run_sync(
agent,   "Inspect the configured fabric folder and write the review report."  ,
max_turns  =  args.max_turns,   run_config  =  RunConfig(  tracing_disabled  =  True  ),
)
except   Exception   as   exc:
(output_dir   /   "partial-run.json"  ).write_text(
json.dumps({  "run_error_type"  :   type  (exc).  __name__  ,   "audit"  : state},   indent  =  2  ),
encoding  =  "utf-8"  ,
)
print  (  f  "Run incomplete (  {type  (exc).  __name__}  ); "
f  "inspect   {  output_dir   /   'partial-run.json'  }  ."  )
return   2
usage   =   result.context_wrapper.usage
requested   =   {(item[  "image_id"  ], hint[  "defect_index"  ])
for   item   in   (state[  "summary"  ]   or   {}).get(  "selected"  , [])
for   hint   in   item[  "hints"  ]}
returned   =   {(v[  "image_id"  ], v[  "defect_index"  ])   for   v   in   state[  "views"  ]}
metrics   =   {
"model"  : args.model,   "workflow"  : args.workflow,   "confidence"  : args.confidence,
"elapsed_seconds"  : time.perf_counter()   -   started,
"input_tokens"  : usage.input_tokens,   "output_tokens"  : usage.output_tokens,
"total_tokens"  : usage.total_tokens,
"screening_called"  : state[  "summary"  ]   is   not   None  ,
"regions_requested"  :   len  (requested),   "regions_returned"  :   len  (returned),
"regions_without_image"  : [  list  (pair)   for   pair   in   sorted  (requested   -   returned)],
}
summary   =   state[  "summary"  ]   or   {}
for   key   in   (  "images_total"  ,   "screened"  ,   "selected_count"  ,   "not_selected"  ):
metrics[key]   =   summary.get(key,   0  )
metrics[  "processing_errors"  ]   =   len  (summary.get(  "processing_errors"  , []))
metrics[  "view_errors"  ]   =   len  (state[  "view_errors"  ])
(output_dir   /   "report.md"  ).write_text(  str  (result.final_output),   encoding  =  "utf-8"  )
for   name, data   in   ((  "audit.json"  , state), (  "usage.json"  , metrics)):
(output_dir   /   name).write_text(json.dumps(data,   indent  =  2  ),   encoding  =  "utf-8"  )
print  (result.final_output)
print  (json.dumps(metrics,   indent  =  2  ))
print  (  f  "Results saved to:   {  output_dir  }  "  )
complete   =   (metrics[  "screening_called"  ]   and   not   metrics[  "regions_without_image"  ]
and   not   metrics[  "processing_errors"  ]   and   not   metrics[  "view_errors"  ])
return   0   if   complete   else   2


if   __name__   ==   "__main__"  :
raise   SystemExit  (main())
```

### Step 5: Evaluate image filtering and agent analysis


We can now compare how the same vision-capable model reviews images with and without filtering. This helps us measure the review workload and examine whether detection metadata helps the model assess a suspected defect.


The optional` compare_review.py` script runs three comparison conditions. All three use full original images:


Condition Images sent to the model Detection metadata


Baseline Every image in the folder None


Filter only Images selected by the Workflow None


Filter with hints The same selected images Predicted classes, confidence scores, bounding boxes, and related metadata


Use the same image folder, model, and reporting instructions for all three runs. The two filtered conditions should read the same` audit.json` so they use exactly the same selected images.


### How the Comparison Works


First, run` fabric_agent.py` as explained in Option 2. It calls the Roboflow Workflow to screen the images and saves the screening results in` audit.json` .


Next, run` compare_review.py` separately for each condition. Without` --audit` , it sends every image to the model. With` --audit` , it reads the saved screening results and sends only the selected images. Adding` --with-hints` also includes their detection metadata.


The comparison script does not run the Workflow again. It reuses the screening results and loads the selected original images from your local folder.


For each run, the model examines the submitted images and writes a visual assessment. The script saves:


- **` report.md`** — image IDs, suspected locations, visible evidence, uncertainty, and suggested next steps for human review.
- **` usage.json`** — the model, comparison condition, number of images submitted, token usage, and review execution time.


**Comparison process for reviewing all images, selected images, and selected images with detection hints.**

### Check Review Quality and Total Workload


For a broader evaluation, use images with verified defect labels. Check whether the Workflow excluded any actual defects and whether the visual review missed or incorrectly reported defects. Record uncertain assessments, unreviewed regions, and processing errors separately.


An unselected image is not automatically defect-free. Compare unselected images with the verified labels and include any additional human review in the workload measurements.

## Conclusion


The Roboflow Workflow gives the AI agent a computer vision tool for textile inspection. It runs object detection, selects images for review, and returns class labels, confidence scores, and bounding boxes. The agent uses these outputs to request visual analysis and generate an inspection report. It can delegate the review to a VLM tool or analyze selected region crops directly.


Use an assistant in ChatGPT or Claude to call both the Workflow and the VLM review tool, or build a Python agent with the OpenAI Agents SDK and` gpt-6-sol` to call the Workflow and analyze returned region crops. Start with a small test set in[Roboflow Workflows (opens in a new tab)](https://docs.roboflow.com/workflows?ref=blog.roboflow.com) , validate the agent's visual assessments, and measure token usage and missed defects before processing larger batches.
